instructions.manual_exchange_notice: Upload this CHATGPT_PACKAGE.json independently in a fresh chat. VideoHoarder never uploads data automatically.

quality_rubric.grounding: Every material transcript-derived conclusion cites canonical segment_ids.
quality_rubric.coverage: Process every exact VIDEO_ID and every requested feature.
quality_rubric.semantic_synthesis: Write semantic summaries that consolidate meaning, argument, method and implications; do not concatenate or lightly rewrite transcript lines.
quality_rubric.timeline: Create boundaries only when the substantive topic changes; merge adjacent fragments about the same point.
quality_rubric.claims: Extract all consequential factual, medical, safety, financial, legal, causal, quantitative and recommendation claims; grade risk and external-verification need.
quality_rubric.entities: Perform named-entity recognition, merge aliases, type entities using the controlled list, and omit generic nouns.
quality_rubric.taxonomy: Use only controlled categories and canonical non-promotional tags.
quality_rubric.editorial: Make assessments specific to this video's evidence, value, limitations and audience; never reuse boilerplate.
quality_rubric.consistency: Use the same canonical evidence across summaries, timeline, claims, intake and editorial assessment.
quality_rubric.specificity: Preserve useful names, quantities, steps and qualifications; avoid generic filler.
quality_rubric.uncertainty: Distinguish source claims, supplied support, interpretation and external-verification needs.
quality_rubric.comments: Cluster only structured supplied comment records and report total, included count and sampling limitations; popularity is not factual verification.
quality_rubric.clips: Select only self-contained clips lasting 30-180 seconds, with valid non-overlapping timestamps and a video-specific purpose.

instructions.instructions: Use only the evidence embedded in this independently processed package and obey response_schema.feature_contracts, controlled_taxonomy, and formal_json_schema. Process every exact VIDEO_ID and return one final JSON object with no prose or markdown. All features must use the same canonical sentence-level transcript segments. Do not claim that you watched or listened to a video. Produce semantic synthesis rather than extractive transcript rewrites. Build timelines from meaningful topic boundaries. Perform complete risk-aware claim extraction and proper named-entity recognition. Make editorial_assessment.v1 a video-specific ChatGPT's Take, not boilerplate. Separate: (1) what the source says, (2) what the supplied evidence supports, (3) your interpretation, and (4) what remains uncertain or requires external verification. Cite canonical transcript segment_ids for transcript-derived conclusions. Downgrade confidence for partial/low evidence. If canonical segments are absent, do not produce transcript-derived summaries, timelines, claims, transcript-derived entities, or clips; metadata/comment-derived fields must identify their source and unsupported fields must be empty/unknown with the limitation. Validate structure, semantics, provenance, duplicates, timestamps, word counts and cross-feature consistency before returning PASS, PASS_WITH_WARNINGS or FAIL.

editorial_assessment.v1.chatgpt_take: A concise, evidence-grounded interpretation—not a repetition of the summary.

practical_value.explanation: Why the material is or is not useful.

credibility_assessment.explanation: Assess presentation and supplied support without pretending to externally fact-check.

editorial_assessment.v1.interpretation_limits: What cannot be concluded from the supplied evidence.

instructions.batch_instruction: This is independently importable batch 35 of 36 in master set vh_batch_set_20260904_090644_7fb4e0. Process only the VIDEO_IDs in this evidence.json. Return one final JSON only for this batch; do not add videos from another batch. This is a NO-TRANSCRIPT package: use only title, description, metadata and comments. Do not invent transcript summaries, timeline sections, timestamps, claims, or clip plans.

rules: Natural English; retain the actual subject
title 5-14 words; short_title 3-8 words
Do not add facts absent from evidence
Use the supplied VideoHoarder categories when one clearly fits; otherwise Other
Prefer specific subjects over generic labels
Return 5-15 deduplicated canonical tags
Each entity has name, type, context, confidence and segment_ids
Allowed types: person, organization, place, product, work, event, concept, law, study, other
Merge aliases and omit generic nouns
Copy total_comments, included_comments and sampling_method from supplied structured comment evidence
Analyze only supplied comment records
Cluster semantically similar comments and report approximate counts
Separate popularity from factual reliability
Quote no more than a short phrase when needed; otherwise paraphrase
Use the supplied evidence assessment as the baseline
Explain downgrades and conflicts
Judge usefulness from supplied evidence only
Do not confuse production popularity with information quality
This is a distinct synthesis, not another summary
overall_score contains score_0_to_100 and explanation
Rewatch sections contain valid timestamps, reason and segment_ids
Separate interpretation from factual verification
Check IDs, provenance, timestamps, contradictions, missing fields and unsupported certainty
FAIL rather than fabricate required content

controlled_taxonomy.tag_rules: lowercase canonical concepts; singular where natural; no promotional filler

response_schema.result_contract: Return ONE JSON object only after processing every exact VIDEO_ID. video_updates must be an array. Each item must include processing_status, evidence_grade, confidence, evidence_references, source_conflicts, validation, and every requested feature using its exact field-level contract and formal_json_schema. Provenance must cite supplied segment_ids when transcript evidence is used. Treat speaker claims as unverified unless external verification is explicitly provided. Use unknown, not_available, or insufficient_evidence instead of inventing content. No automatic deletion, file movement, clipping, or upload.

metadata.description:
Which is  the Best Sunscreen in the Indian Market? 

Summer is round the corner and in this season the one cream that should be a part of your daily cosmetic kit is a sunscreen. Sun is the source of energy on this planet, however prolonged exposure to the UV rays of the sun may lead to sunburn, fast ageing and in some cases even skin cancer. So applying a sunscreen on a daily basis becomes extremely important. However, it is shocking that most commercial sunscreens in the market are full of toxic chemicals like oxybenzone, parabens, mineral oil, BHT and many others which not only harm the skin but also completely block the absorption of the Vitamin D in the body, of which the sun is a major source.
So, what choice do we have? Obviously, we want to protect ourselves from the harmful radiations of the sun but at the same time we don’t want a toxic sunscreen to damage our skin. 

In search of the best sunscreen in the Indian market I picked up almost 15 sunscreens, some from the supermarket while others online.
After an in-depth analysis, I have sorted out all these sunscreens into 3 categories on the basis of number of toxic chemicals present in them.

01:42 - CATEGORY #1 - These sunscreen creams have 10 or more toxic chemicals in them. Many of these chemicals have been known to interfere with the thyroid gland. Some of these chemicals have the capacity to cross the skin and get into other tissues in the body. Basically, they are the worst in the market.

02:33 - CATEGORY #2 - These sunscreens claim to be non cosmetic and Ayurvedic but it does not mention the complete list of ingredients. However, they do contain some harmful chemicals.

03:33 - What is Sun Protection Factor (SPF) number really means?

04:35 - CATEGORY #3 - Sunscreens by these brands have nothing to hide as they have mentioned the complete list of ingredients. These sunscreens are safe and natural in their true sense.
